MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including a recent focus on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Builds GitLab CI workflows and Helm-based ephemeral environments for three product teams, with measurable improvements in pipeline duration and test stability. Developing toward a full-time DevOps / platform engineering role, with additional hands-on personal experience using Terraform, k3s and GitOps.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure and CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform (personal project)
Platforms and observability: Kubernetes (namespace-level access; Helm deployments to a shared cluster), k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki
Programming and data: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman, Linux, Git, Ansible (basic)
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)

EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, plus artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner cost fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived, per-merge-request test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster; environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built a Python and PostgreSQL test-results pipeline and Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and authored the internal CI guide used in onboarding.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated approaches.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED PROJECT
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal project | 2024–2025
- Ran a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, deploying applications from a Git repository with Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, with Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Preparing for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam, scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. My background combines CI/CD ownership, repeatable test environments and a practical focus on making systems more reliable—experience I would bring to the infrastructure work supporting Corvale’s new train fleet.

At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and built short-lived, per-merge-request environments deployed with Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and helped lower the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%. I also wrote the internal guide to how the CI system works, which is used in onboarding. These projects have involved improving workflows across teams and making infrastructure easier to use and understand.

Alongside my professional work, I built a personal three-node k3s homelab with GitOps deployment through Argo CD, monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, and Terraform provisioning for a small Hetzner VPS. This gives me additional hands-on experience with infrastructure automation and observability. I am interested in Corvale’s challenge of shaping the platform that connects train systems with cloud services, where reliability, security and clear interfaces matter.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my infrastructure-focused experience and continued development toward platform engineering could contribute to the fleet connectivity team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Marta Kowal-Brandt
